_source.description: Major global tin mining, smelting, and processing sites
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 — Tin chapter (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); International Tin Association production statistics (internationaltin.org); PT Timah Tbk Annual Report 2023 (timah.com); Yunnan Tin Group Annual Report 2023; Minsur S.A. Annual Report 2023 (minsur.com); Alphamin Resources NI 43-101 Technical Report 2023 (alphaminresources.com); Metals X Ltd ASX filings; COMIBOL (Bolivia) production reports; Myanmar Mines Department statistics; Malaysia Smelting Corporation (MSC) Annual Report 2023; S&P Global Market Intelligence mine database; British Geological Survey World Mineral Production data
_source.license: USGS: public domain; ITA: public statistics; company data: fair use summary; BGS: Open Government Licence
_source.notes: Major tin mining and smelting operations worldwide. Global tin supply is concentrated in SE Asia and China. Myanmar production (largely from Wa State) is difficult to verify independently. Coordinates from company filings, NI 43-101 reports, satellite imagery, and USGS MRDS.

_coverage.known_gaps: Myanmar artisanal and small-scale tin mining in Shan State and Wa State accounts for ~11% of global supply but individual mines cannot be reliably mapped; Indonesian offshore tin dredging operations (numerous small vessels) are not individually captured; Chinese tin recycling facilities (~15% of domestic supply) not included; Rwandan artisanal tantalite-tin operations are fragmented across many small sites

sites.name: PT Timah (Bangka Island — Pemali)
sites.notes: PT Timah is the world's largest integrated tin miner. Primary operations on Bangka Island, numerous dredges and open-pit mines. PT Timah produced ~25,000-30,000 t Sn in 2023.

sites.name: PT Timah (Bangka Island — Sungailiat)
sites.notes: Northern Bangka dredging operations. Includes onshore and offshore alluvial tin dredges.

sites.name: PT Babel Tin (Bangka Island)
sites.ownership: PT RBT / various private Indonesian miners
sites.notes: Private-sector tin mining on Bangka. PT RBT is a major private smelter. Numerous small miners supply concentrate.

sites.name: Belitung Island Tin Mines
sites.notes: Belitung Island (historically 'Billiton') — one of the world's historic tin mining centers. Alluvial deposits now partially depleted.

sites.name: PT Timah Smelter (Mentok, Bangka)
sites.notes: PT Timah's primary tin smelter at Mentok, western Bangka. Produces LME-grade tin ingots.

sites.name: Gejiu Tin Mines (Yunnan Tin Group)
sites.notes: World's largest tin mining complex. 'Tin Capital' of China. Gejiu has been mined for tin for over 2,000 years. Yunnan Tin Group is the world's largest tin producer by output.

sites.name: Yunnan Tin Smelter (Gejiu)
sites.notes: World's largest tin smelter. YTC's refinery at Gejiu processes concentrates from domestic mines and imports.

sites.name: Dachang Tin Mine (Guangxi)
sites.notes: One of the world's largest tin deposits. Located in Nandan County, Guangxi. Contains tin-zinc-lead polymetallic ores.

sites.name: Hunan Nonferrous Tin Operations
sites.notes: Tin-tungsten mining operations in Hunan province, southern China.

sites.name: Jiangxi Tin Mines
sites.notes: Jiangxi province is a significant tin producing region. Numerous small and mid-size underground tin-tungsten mines.

sites.name: Man Maw Mine (Wa State)
sites.notes: Major tin-tungsten deposit in the Wa Self-Administered Division. Discovered ~2008, rapidly expanded. Most output exported to China for smelting. Governance and ESG concerns — controlled by UWSA militia.

sites.name: Shan State Tin Mines (Kayah cluster)
sites.notes: Scattered tin mining operations in Shan State. Much smaller than Man Maw. Difficult to verify production due to ongoing conflict.

sites.name: San Rafael Mine (Puno)
sites.notes: Western Hemisphere's largest tin mine, at 4,500m elevation in the Andes. Minsur produced ~20,000-22,000 t Sn in 2023. Very high grade by global standards.

sites.name: Minsur Pisco Smelter
sites.notes: Minsur's FUNSUR tin smelter at Pisco on Peru's coast. One of the world's purest tin producers. Processes San Rafael concentrate.

sites.name: Bisie Mine (Alphamin)
sites.notes: World's highest-grade operational tin mine. Located in North Kivu province. Alphamin produced ~12,000 t Sn concentrate in 2023. Mpama South expansion completed 2023.

sites.name: Huanuni Mine
sites.notes: Bolivia's largest tin mine. State-owned and operated by COMIBOL since nationalization. Historic mine dating to colonial era.

sites.name: San Jose Mine (Oruro)
sites.notes: Cooperative-worked tin and silver mine in Oruro department. Typical of Bolivia's cooperative mining sector.

sites.name: Vinto Smelter (Oruro)
sites.notes: Bolivia's only tin smelter, nationalized from Glencore in 2007. Located at ~3,700m elevation. Processes domestic concentrate.

sites.name: Pitinga Mine (Taboca/Minsur)
sites.notes: Remote tin-niobium-tantalum mine in the Amazon rainforest, Amazonas state. One of the world's largest tin resources. Also a major niobium and tantalum source.

sites.name: Mamore Smelter (Sao Paulo)
sites.notes: Taboca/Minsur's tin smelter near Sao Paulo. Processes Pitinga mine concentrate.

sites.name: Renison Bell Mine
sites.ownership: Metals X / Yunnan Tin Australia (50/50 JV)
sites.notes: Australia's only operating tin mine. Located in western Tasmania. One of the world's largest and highest-grade hard-rock tin deposits. Metals X/Yunnan Tin JV.

sites.name: Mt Bischoff (Tasmania)
sites.notes: Historic tin mine in NW Tasmania. Under redevelopment. Australia's first tin mine (1871). Mt Bischoff was once the world's richest tin mine.

sites.name: Malaysia Smelting Corporation (Butterworth)
sites.notes: One of the world's largest and oldest tin smelters (founded 1887 in Penang). Processes concentrates from multiple countries. MSC is a globally significant custom smelter.

sites.name: Rahman Hydraulic Tin (Perak)
sites.notes: Malaysia's last significant tin mining operation. Open-pit alluvial mining in Perak state, once the world's top tin-producing region.

sites.name: Jos Plateau Tin Mines
sites.notes: Historic tin-mining region on the Jos Plateau. Largely artisanal since the decline of large-scale mining. Nigeria was once a major tin exporter.

sites.name: Rutongo Mines (Kigali)
sites.notes: Rwanda is Africa's second-largest tin producer (after DRC). Cassiterite mining from pegmatite veins and alluvial deposits. Subject to ITSCI traceability scheme.

sites.name: Nyakabingo Mine
sites.notes: Tin and tungsten mine in northwest Rwanda. Part of the Great Lakes conflict minerals supply chain — ITSCI-tagged.

sites.name: Thaisarco Smelter (Phuket)
sites.notes: Major custom tin smelter on Phuket island. Processes concentrates from across SE Asia and Africa. LME-registered brand.

sites.name: Mandalay Tin Smelter
sites.notes: Tin smelting cluster near Mandalay processing Wa State mine concentrates. Some material exported as concentrate to Yunnan Tin in China.

sites.name: Guangxi Tin Smelter (Hechi)
sites.notes: Tin smelter in Hechi, Guangxi province. Processes Dachang mine concentrates and purchased material.

sites.name: Potosi Tin Mines (Llallagua)
sites.notes: Historic tin mining district (Catavi-Siglo XX-Llallagua complex). Once the world's largest tin producer in the early 20th century under Simon Patino.

sites.name: Achmmach Tin Project
sites.notes: Tin development project in the Middle Atlas Mountains. One of the few tin projects in North Africa. Bankable feasibility study completed.
